column1: # The status line the CLI draws under its input box.
# The launcher sends nothing to a session until the pane ends in the input
# box with one of these lines under it:
#     ❯                              the input, opened by the prompt glyph
#       ⏵⏵ accept edits on …         the status line: a row of this table
# The box is recognised by its shape and by being at the foot of the pane.
# This table is the second half of the evidence: the line under the box has
# to be a status line. Text that only appears somewhere on the pane is not
# evidence: a dialog can quote a status line and a shell can echo one.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   id       short name
#   pattern  how the status line begins, mode symbol included
#   basis    seen      drawn by the real CLI in a pane, and read from it
#            inferred  built by the same rule as the rows that were seen, or
#                      taken from another release, and not seen
# A line matches a row when it starts with the pattern. A narrow pane cuts
# the line short ("⏵⏵ accept edits" at 20 columns, "⏵⏵" at 12), and a cut
# line matches when what is left is the start of the pattern and holds at
# least the symbol. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
# The rows marked seen were drawn by CLI 2.1.330, started in a pseudo-terminal
# with no credentials and a temporary home directory, at 100 columns; the
# accept-edits row also at 40, 25, 20, 16 and 12, replayed through tmux 3.3a.
# The bypass row is inferred. Starting the CLI with permissions bypassed to
# look at it is refused in this repository, on purpose. In that release the
# mode's title is "Bypass Permissions", its symbol is the one accept-edits
# uses, and every seen row is the symbol, the title in lower case, and "on".
# If a session launched with --bypass is at its prompt and the launcher says
# the prompt never appeared, this is the row to correct.
# The shortcuts row is inferred too: 2.1.330 draws that hint after the mode
# ("⏸ manual mode on · ? for shortcuts"), and releases that drew no mode for
# the default one began the line with it.
accept-edits
bypass
plan
auto
dont-ask
manual
shortcuts
